NEXORA — FULL-SYSTEM FORENSIC AUDIT, REPAIR, SECURITY HARDENING, AND VERIFIED ACCEPTANCE PROMPT
Version 1.0 | Prepared from uploaded untitled.zip | Audit snapshot: 2026-11-03

========================================================================================================================
0. ROLE, AUTHORITY, AND NON-NEGOTIABLE OUTCOME
========================================================================================================================

Act as principal application engineer, security engineer, backend architect, database/rules engineer, QA lead, accessibility reviewer, and release engineer for the NEXORA Enterprise Operations Cloud repository supplied with this prompt.

THIS IS AN IMPLEMENTATION TASK, NOT A REVIEW-ONLY TASK. Inspect the complete repository, identify every broken, inert, misleading, insecure, incomplete, or fake capability, repair the actual source files, create missing functionality and tests, run available checks, and return verifiable evidence. Do not return only a plan, explanation, snippets, mockup, or list of suggestions. The final result must be a coherent working application, not a visually convincing collection of buttons and toasts.

Inspect every file, nested directory, source module, duplicate implementation, deployment adapter, config file, rule, generated artifact, test, and document. Do not restrict review to index.html. Do not assume an earlier AI-generated plan, README checklist, generated bundle, checked box, test count, or success toast proves that a feature works.

EVIDENCE-BASED COMPLETION STANDARD
- A UI control is complete only if its intended action actually occurs, is validated and authorized, persists when applicable, is reflected from authoritative state, survives reload, and handles failure correctly.
- A backend operation is complete only if authentication, authorization, tenant scoping, schema validation, atomicity/idempotency where needed, durable persistence, and tests all work.
- A diagnostic is complete only if it executes the named test and reports the actual result. A canned PASS is a defect.
- A prototype/simulation/demo must be unmistakably labelled and isolated from production data and operations.
- A failure must never become success because of a swallowed exception, empty-array fallback, mock fixture, arbitrary default, optimistic state, or toast.
- Production capability must never rely only on client checks, hidden buttons, localStorage, request-body role/UID/orgId, or browser-supplied consent.
- Do not claim perfection. Report actual test evidence, external blockers, and residual risks honestly.

ZERO-TOLERANCE RULES
1. No knowingly broken, inert, misleading, fake, or showpiece production controls.
2. No fake API responses, test results, metrics, audit logs, workflow execution, invitations, emails, payment state, or database writes.
3. No privileges based on client-supplied role, UID, email, org ID, demo flag, consent flag, or userData.
4. No fail-open behavior for authentication, membership, authorization, billing, entitlements, Firestore, signature verification, or tenant resolution.
5. No leakage of API keys, provider credentials, Firebase Admin credentials, webhook secrets, bearer tokens, exception internals, or private customer data.
6. No swallowed failures. Show a safe user error, log correlated server-side evidence, and preserve retryability.
7. A webhook is not PROCESSED until all required durable mutations succeed or a recoverable processing state is written.
8. No stale or fabricated values as live business data.
9. Do not blank out or re-scaffold the app, discard working modules, or downgrade NEXORA to avoid understanding it.
10. Do not merely hide a failed feature while leaving misleading claims elsewhere.
11. Preserve valid user data and original business meaning.
12. Never ask the user to paste secrets into chat. Read secrets only from secure environment variables and report missing variable names, never values.
13. Never test by charging, refunding, emailing, or mutating real production users.
14. Continue through every repository area and test matrix case; do not stop after finding a large defect.
15. A successful TypeScript build alone does not establish functionality or security.

========================================================================================================================
2. PRIORITIES AND EXECUTION ORDER
========================================================================================================================

P0 — critical identity, privilege, tenant isolation, consent, secrets, webhook, billing, entitlement, destructive-operation, or data-integrity risk. Must be fixed before production.
P1 — broken/no-op controls, false-success behavior, missing route, missing persistence, fake metrics, incomplete CRUD, deceptive diagnostics, or route/deployment mismatch. Must be fixed before calling the app functional.
P2 — accessibility, performance, resilience, observability, maintainability, and edge-case quality. Fix before release where feasible.

Execution order:
1. Freeze production mutation tests; establish safe emulator/mocked environment.
2. Inventory repository, controls, routes, and all adapters.
3. Fix P0 auth, membership, org scoping, consent, webhook, billing, entitlement, token exposure.
4. Fix backend service contracts and route parity.
5. Fix Firestore model/rules and safe migration.
6. Fix front-end persistence, CRUD, edit, and truthful feedback.
7. Implement or honestly disable/label workflows, invites, notifications, diagnostics, and integrations.
8. Fix analytics, dates, charts, AI provenance, and finance calculations.
9. Fix accessibility/mobile/performance/error handling.
10. Run unit, rules, API, browser, security, concurrency, and build checks.
11. Update documentation to match actual code.
12. Deliver a repair ledger and evidence-based release verdict.

========================================================================================================================
3. HIGH-PRIORITY SOURCE FINDINGS — VERIFY AND REPAIR
========================================================================================================================

These are concrete observations from the uploaded source snapshot. Re-open and verify current source before editing. Each is a required audit item, not a substitute for further inspection.

3.1 IDENTITY, SESSION, TENANT BOOTSTRAP
- index.html around 538–554 contains fallback user identity/name and a role fallback of OWNER. Remove production fallbacks. Missing auth means unauthenticated; missing membership means no tenant access, never OWNER.
- index.html around 587–606 contains switchSimulatedUser(), which replaces currentUser without Firebase Auth. Simulated identities may only exist inside isolated demo mode. Live mode must not expose impersonation controls or trust a simulated UID/role.
- index.html around 1656–1796 derives org ID from only the first 16 alphanumeric UID characters. Replace with trusted server-side organization/membership resolution or collision-resistant canonical mapping. A derived ID does not prove membership.
- syncLiveOrg() appears to create new orgs and seed live project/task collections with hard-coded demo fixtures. It sets currentRole='OWNER' before membership resolution and can fabricate OWNER membership when member lookup is empty or fails. This is critical. Remove all synthetic live seeding and owner fallback. Create tenant only through explicit authorized server operation. Resolve active membership before setting role/loading private data. Failed lookup must deny access, never imply empty membership means owner.
- Support multiple organizations per user, accepted invitations, removed membership, suspended account/org, and explicit org selection. Do not assume one user = one owned org.
- Org switcher around index.html 6621–6644 shows one fixed organization, SCALE/OWNER labels, and a button that only closes the modal and toasts “Organization creation wizard initialized.” Implement real tenant list/select/provisioning or visibly mark unavailable and remove misleading action. Revalidate selection server-side and clear old tenant caches/listeners.

3.2 PERSISTENCE AND FALSE SUCCESS
- saveToFirestore() around 1590–1603 and updateInFirestore() around 1605–1629 swallow persistence failures through catch handlers. Callers then often show success. Make persistence return typed outcomes or throw. No success toast/close/authoritative local mutation until confirmed.
- updateInFirestore() appears to setDoc a record if update target is missing. Separate create/update/upsert. Update missing record must return NOT_FOUND unless explicit upsert behavior is documented.
- Many create/update operations mutate demoStore/liveStore before confirmed Firestore write. Use pending state and rollback or update only from authoritative result. Prevent double-submit.
- refreshLiveData() around 1647–1654 always shows “Cloud sync complete!” even if syncLiveOrg swallowed errors. Return per-collection sync statuses and show partial/error state truthfully.
- Search all callers/catches/fallbacks (`|| []`, `|| {}`, hard-coded numbers) and all unconditional success toasts.
- IDs made from the last four digits of Date.now() can collide. Use Firestore-generated IDs or cryptographically strong IDs, tenant scope, and idempotency. Use server timestamps for authoritative fields.

3.3 ACTIVITY AND AUDIT
- recordActivity() around 1631–1645 prepends only to client arrays, appears not to persist, and uses actorName without actorUid.
- firestore.rules around 524–530 requires actorUid == request.auth.uid on activityEvents create. Current event shape is incompatible with that rule if a write is attempted; activity may be only local UI state.
- Build a server-authoritative, append-only audit service with immutable ID, org, actor UID/role snapshot, event type, entity, action, server time, correlation ID, source, outcome, and sanitized diff when appropriate. Do not log secrets or unnecessary PII.
- Each successful high-impact operation should emit one durable audit event. Retries must not duplicate. Activity UI must query persisted events with pagination, filters, permission checks, and accurate empty/error states.

3.4 AI AUTH, CONSENT, DATA, PROPOSALS
- index.html 556–585 stores consent in localStorage first, attempts Firestore write, swallows errors, and still shows grant/revoke success. LocalStorage is not server consent. Implement server-authoritative consent with UID, org, policy version, purpose, timestamp, revocation timestamp and audit. Failure must not show success; revocation must apply immediately.
- sendAiCopilotMessage() around 928–1059 appears to send client role/org/permissionGranted/userData. Backend must ignore client claims for principal, role, membership, consent, data and tenant. Derive UID from verified ID token; resolve current active membership and consent; load only allowed records server-side.
- functions/src/ai/copilotService.ts around 489–524 appears to allow client permissionGranted or supplied userData to bypass required Bearer authentication; it treats those values as consent too. Remove this path. Every live request must require valid token, active user, active membership, permission, and server consent. Demo mode must use server-verifiable demo session or be static/local with no live API access.
- Request body userId/userRole/orgId/demoMode/permissionGranted/userData are untrusted. Never use them for identity, rate-limit scope or tenant data selection.
- Rate limiter around 156–182 appears to use in-memory Map keyed by request identity. Serverless instances do not share it; clients can rotate spoofed IDs. Use distributed atomic rate limit keyed by verified UID plus org/global budgets.
- Copilot around 530–583 appears to add synthetic records when consented data is empty. Live mode must never inject fixtures. Empty DB -> honest no records; failed query -> data-source error. Keep mock data exclusively inside labelled DemoDataProvider.
- Copilot around 591–606 appears to add arbitrary +15000 burn and $340000 cash to compute runway. Remove these live-mode constants. Use the integer-cent finance engine and real tenant records. Missing sources -> UNKNOWN/INSUFFICIENT_DATA, not guessed result.
- Review system prompt for claims of full access. Provide exact source provenance, data freshness, query coverage, missing fields and limits. Model must state uncertainty and not invent.
- A blocked-field blacklist around lines 141/750 is inadequate. Use per-collection allowlists, strict schemas, field-level authorization, nested validation, immutable fields, status transition tables, tenant binding and expected document version. Reject unknown collection/path, nested protected keys, prototype keys and unapproved fields.
- Proposal fallback around 776–799 appears to fabricate req-501 when no matching record exists. Never invent IDs. Return not-found/clarification.
- approveAndApplyProposal() around 1070–1126 appears to apply mutations directly from browser and keep proposal state locally. Persist proposal server-side, with verified creator, tenant, source, provenance, allowed action, payload hash, expiry and state. Approval must recheck human identity/permission, record version and allowlist, atomically apply, persist audit, and be idempotent. Decline must persist after reload.
- AI key remains server-side. Restrict base URL/model, set timeouts, output size and token budget; safely parse output; map upstream errors; correlate requests; avoid logging private prompts.

3.5 FIRESTORE RULES AND TENANT SECURITY
- firestore.rules 23–26 includes public read on /test/{testId}. Remove production public read or isolate it to disposable test project and authenticated test identity.
- isPlatformAdmin() around 33–43 has hard-coded UID/email/placeholder. Replace sole identity authority with server-managed custom claims or protected audited registry; email text alone is not authorization. Bootstrap through trusted one-time process.
- isOrgMember() around 70–77 appears to test membership existence/ownerUid without consistently requiring status ACTIVE, active account, active org. All business reads/writes need active user + active membership + active org, except explicit platform-admin paths.
- isUserActive() around 110–116 appears inconsistently applied. Audit every match path and centralize active checks.
- member rules around 213–228 appear to accept existence of invitation doc ID without binding invite to verified email/UID, org, pending state, expiry, revocation, one-time status and role. Knowing token doc ID may be enough to create a privileged member. Replace with server-mediated one-time atomic redemption; store hashed token; bind org, intended identity, role, expiry; never trust client-selected role.
- Same member rules appear to allow broad admin update with possible ORG_ADMIN -> OWNER promotion. Only current owner/platform admin may assign OWNER; define atomic ownership transfer, no self-role editing, immutable UID/org/role fields, auditable changes.
- Proposal rules around 243–269 need immutable creator/org/target/status/provenance, strict allowed transitions and approver authorization. Prefer server-side mutation.
- Review all collection matches: projects, tasks, requests, incidents, goals, customers/accounts, vendors, assets, knowledge, meetings, workflows, data quality, members, proposals, activityEvents, notifications, billing, integrations, platform. Define exact read/create/update/delete per role and schema.
- Notifications around 536–540 appear to allow members to create notifications and recipient to update. Validate sender authority and immutable recipient/source/org. Prefer server-created notifications; only allow recipient to update narrowly allowed read state.
- activityEvents requires actorUid == auth.uid; align server writes and make append-only.
- Admin SDK bypasses Firestore rules. Server routes must independently enforce every org/role check.
- inquiries appears to have no explicit Firestore rule and default deny. Do not add broad write access. Implement server inquiry endpoint with validation, anti-spam, rate limiting and honest notification, or label submission unavailable.
- Keep firestore.rules and public/firestore.rules.txt (and any copied rule artifacts) synchronized from one canonical source/generator. CI must diff. Emulator positive and negative rules tests required.

3.6 WEBHOOK, BILLING, ENTITLEMENTS
- functions/src/billing/webhook.ts includes unsafeUnwrap(rawBody) around line 113 as fallback. Never accept unverified production webhook. If signing key missing, reject and do not mutate state. Verify exact raw bytes with official SDK and required headers.
- Enforce timestamp replay tolerance; require valid provider event ID and signature. Do not synthesize trusted ID using Date.now().
- Current idempotency appears check-then-write/non-atomic and may swallow Firestore errors then mark processed. Implement atomic state: RECEIVED -> PROCESSING with lease/version -> PROCESSED only after durable success; FAILED_RETRYABLE for transient errors; QUARANTINED for invalid/unmatched. Concurrent duplicates must have one logical effect.
- Never acknowledge as processed if required billing mutation failed unless a durable queue owns retry. Store unmatched events for reconciliation and alert. Do not silently discard unknown event types.
- Verify subscription/customer/org association, product ID, amount, currency, status, event ordering and metadata. A signed metadata field alone must not redirect an event across tenants; verify stored checkout/subscription association.
- resolvePlanFromDodoProductId() in plans.ts appears to use substring heuristics and may default unknown product to STARTER. Exact ID mapping only; unknown product quarantined and no paid access.
- verifyOrgBillingAccess() in firebaseAuth.ts appears to derive UID-prefix org, trust hard-coded owner email, and synthesize active org when reads fail. Fail closed on every Firestore failure and resolve real active membership/role.
- getOrgEntitlements() appears to catch read failures and default to FREE/ACTIVE-like state. Distinguish unknown/unavailable from actual plan; never grant active paid entitlement due to read failure. Avoid destructive downgrade on transient outage; require reconciliation.
- checkFeature/usage API must authorize org membership; changing orgId cannot expose plan, usage or invoices.
- Usage limits must be server-side, atomic and concurrency-safe. Validate delta positive safe integer; reject zero/negative/NaN/Infinity. Cover seats/projects/workflows/storage/AI credits/automations and all caps.
- Checkout/plan-change/preview/cancel/reactivate/portal require idempotency, state validation and trusted return URL allowlist. Provider success + DB failure must enter recovery/reconciliation, never false success.
- Use integer minor units and ISO 4217 currency. No float money or default `$` assumptions.
- Audit owner actions, bulk actions, plan changes, webhook retry, flags and destructive operations.

3.7 API PARITY, CORS, SERVERLESS
- Compare route registrations in server.ts, netlify/functions/api.ts, functions/src/index.ts. Snapshot suggests local Express and Netlify contain /api/owner/* and /api/ai/*, while Firebase index may export billing only. firebase.json rewrites /api/** to Firebase `api`, so owner/AI routes may 404 in Firebase despite working local/Netlify. Verify and fix route parity or explicitly prevent deployment with unsupported features. Do not ship buttons that depend on missing deployment routes.
- Avoid three duplicated business implementations. Extract common services and keep adapters thin. Share validation/auth/tenant/error semantics. Run contract parity tests.
- server.ts appears to use cors origin true; Netlify appears Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Use exact configured origin allowlist, Vary: Origin, safe credentials handling and explicit methods/headers. Validate config at startup.
- Reject malformed JSON; enforce content-type, body size, schemas, unknown-field policy, timeouts, pagination caps, exact status codes.
- Netlify errorResponse() appears to expose err.message. Return stable safe error code/message; detailed error server-side only with correlation ID. No internal paths/provider details/stack/secrets.
- Remove or carefully scope global uncaughtException/unhandledRejection recovery in serverless; do not keep serving after unhandled process corruption.
- Each route needs declared auth, permission, tenant scope, schema, rate limit, response, audit and idempotency contract.
- Add CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors and private cache directives. Design CSP without breaking inline app; prefer move to controlled bundle or hashes/nonces rather than broad unsafe policies.
- Verify CDN scripts and unpinned Lucide @latest usage; pin/review dependencies, use SRI/self-host critical assets, ensure Tailwind production CSS is built locally.
- Audit firebase.json/netlify.toml/Vite paths/runtime/lockfiles/.firebaserc/deploy ignore. Never deploy .env, credentials, internal prompts, test fixture PII, or secrets in source maps.

3.8 DIAGNOSTICS — DECEPTIVE AUDIT BEHAVIOR
- index.html around 6737–6916 has runDeepAudit() whose checks appear shallow/unconditional: WebSocket waits and passes without testing; health failure may still pass; any auth response except 401 may pass; webhook check may pass on wrong failures; tenant isolation compares static DB ID; XSS tests only call escapeHtml; storage tests localStorage only; chart checks only `typeof Chart`; FPS is short RAF loop with clamping.
- It appears always to report “ALL 10 VERIFICATION AUDIT CHECKS PASSED (100% HEALTHY)” regardless of failure. Remove. Each check must actually execute and return PASS/FAIL/WARN/SKIP with prerequisite, action, exact expected result, actual status/measurements, evidence, timestamp, and safe message. SKIP never counts as PASS; partial suite never shows 100%.
- Use finally to restore button state; add timeout/cancel; never freeze UI or mutate live data.
- Export around 6918–6945 appears hard-coded 100% PASS. Export actual run/checks/status/evidence, redact secrets, and handle clipboard/download failure.
- Remove false production claim “Vite WebSocket Isolated & Clean” unless an actual check is valid in that environment.

3.9 WORKFLOW CANVAS
- addWorkflowNode() around 8091–8100 appears only to log activity and toast; it does not add a graph node. Implement real typed node in graph state, unique ID, config, rendering, selection, inspector, connections, delete, undo/redo and serialization.
- saveWorkflowDraft() around 8057–8072 appears to write hard-coded wf-1/name/version, not the current graph, and may show success in demo even with no persistence. Save real graph, validate schema, version and concurrency; label demo local draft honestly.
- publishWorkflow() around 8074–8089 appears to write fixed wf-1 version/status without graph compilation, validation or executable deployment. README says server workflow worker/background runtime is future work. Do not claim workflow deployed/executing unless an actual worker exists. If unavailable, show published-definition or execution-disabled state, not live runtime.
- README differentiates visual designer/client simulation from future worker/cron/wait/API polling. Preserve this distinction. Simulation must never cause external side effects. Live worker requires retries, idempotency, execution history, permission revalidation, secret handling, cancellation, monitoring.

3.10 DASHBOARD / ANALYTICS / SYNTHETIC DATA
- renderCommandCenter and charts around index.html 2447+, 6301–6475 contain fixed labels/values such as “3 On Track · 1 Watch”, “78.4% Sprint Velocity”, “Avg 18.5h turnaround”, “P1 Webhook Timeout”, “+14.2% MoM”, and fixed chart series. Verify all. Live values must derive from persisted authorized tenant records. Empty data -> accurate empty/zero/insufficient state, not samples.
- Fixed bottleneck/alert cards must point to real records or be labelled demo. Incident card requires matching actual incident.
- Date range must affect every KPI/chart/table/insight. Define timezone, start-inclusive/end-exclusive boundaries, DST, current and comparison periods.
- Share aggregation definitions across dashboard, analytics, exports, finance and AI.
- Implement chart loading/empty/error, units, labels, accessible descriptions, tooltip, resize cleanup and destruction. No duplicate chart instances.
- Clear/scope caches by tenant/UID/permission/range/version so org switch cannot show old tenant values.

3.11 ENTITY CRUD, VALIDATION, EDIT MODALS
- Inspect every open*Modal/saveNew*/update/delete/archive handler. Some account/asset/goal/knowledge/meeting modal functions may ignore IDs and always create; prove whether edit flow loads the selected record.
- Project create around 6989–7032: short timestamp ID, writes to both demoStore/liveStore, fake owner fallback, parseInt budget and default date; verify persistence and success.
- Task create around 7071+: sample project ID, synthetic assignee, fixed hours and stale default date 2026-10-15 (snapshot audit date 2026-11-03); verify correct real references and validation.
- Request create around 7144–7180: synthetic approver UID, parseInt amount without robust finite/positive validation and hard-coded values; remove.
- Incident create around 7217–7252 contains hard-coded impact/root-cause/mitigation claims about probes/failsafe without evidence; make factual.
- advanceTaskStatus around 7254–7276 mutates local before server and may falsely succeed; enforce server transition/version.
- decideRequest around 7278–7298 must validate decision allowlist and role/state server-side.
- resolveIncident around 7300–7320 needs permission, resolution summary, timestamp and durable state.
- submitEnterpriseInquiry() around 7686–7709 appears to write `inquiries`, which has no explicit rule, then claim an architect is assigned within two business hours. Implement server workflow or remove false claim.
- Meeting save appears to claim calendar invites dispatched. Verify provider; if none, only save internal meeting and clearly state no invite sent.
- Validate all form required fields, enum, Unicode, max lengths, emails, phone, URL protocol, date/timezone, integer amount, currency, references, uploads and duplicates. Client check is only usability; server revalidates.
- Edit form must load actual record, show identity, dirty state, warn before discard, use optimistic concurrency, field errors, keep values on failure, refresh canonical data.
- Delete/archive needs target confirmation, permission, retention/reference checks, soft delete if required, audit, idempotency and correct list refresh.

3.12 NOTIFICATIONS / SETTINGS
- markAllNotificationsRead() around 8135–8144 appears to mutate local arrays only. Persist recipient read state. Immutable recipient/sender/source/org/message/createdAt; reload and second device must match.
- saveOrgSettings() around 8105–8130 appears to mutate currentOrg before Firestore, swallow errors, and always toast “committed to Firestore.” Store canonical IANA zone and ISO currency, validate role, persist, rollback failure, toast only after confirmation.

3.13 API BASE URL / TOKEN SAFETY
- apiBaseUrl/setApiBaseUrl around 8150–8180 accepts localStorage endpoint and appears to block only some external hosts. Search every fetch for Authorization header/token. If user can point base URL at hostile origin, signed-in bearer token may be exfiltrated.
- Production base URL must come from trusted deploy config or strict allowlist. If dev-only custom URL exists, gate it, warn, and never attach credentials to untrusted origin. Enforce HTTPS, origin/path allowlist, and redirect restrictions. Do not forward ID token cross-origin.

3.14 XSS / ACCESSIBILITY / ERROR HANDLING
- index.html uses template strings and innerHTML extensively. Audit every dynamic sink including Firestore, AI, notification, profiles, task/vendor/notes, filenames, errors, URLs, config. Use textContent/DOM APIs where possible; contextually escape; validate URL protocols; never interpolate untrusted data into inline onclick.
- Consent modal around line 688 appears to interpolate userName without escapeHtml. Verify and fix; audit titles, href, attributes, data attributes, SVG and JS strings. Unit test of escapeHtml alone is insufficient; DOM XSS tests required.
- Early script around 14–138 appears to intercept console errors/browser errors/unhandledrejection and fake Vite HMR WebSocket. Remove production suppression/fake HMR; preserve genuine error telemetry with redaction.
- initTheme() around 391–403 adds matchMedia listener every call; setTheme invokes it repeatedly. Register once and clean up.
- openModal around 464–488 needs dialog role/label, focus entry/trap/restore, Escape, background inert, scroll lock, nested dialog and unsaved change handling. Audit global Escape behavior.
- All buttons/inputs/tables/charts need accessible names, labels, errors, focus, semantic structure, text alternatives, and reduced-motion handling. Test touch, 320px width, landscape, zoom 200%, large text and soft keyboard.

3.15 README/BUILD/TEST TRUTH
- README claims security/feature readiness but also labels workflow worker and email adapter as future backend. Align all claims with source; remove unproven zero-hallucination/full-access/secure/live-dispatch assertions.
- A previous implementation plan appears to claim “187/187 tests passing”; current scripts/test-verification.ts appears to contain far fewer literal assert sites and uses loops. Run it and report actual executed case count; documentation is not evidence.
- Root package.json has TypeScript in devDependencies in supplied snapshot; verify actual tsconfig/build rather than repeat outdated assumptions.
- node_modules absent in extracted archive at initial review; do not claim build/test run. Use reproducible lockfile install in sandbox.
- src/App.tsx seems to return an empty div while index.html holds application. Determine actual built entry before any refactor; never accidentally replace the app with blank UI.
- test-bundle.cjs is large generated output. Verify provenance and staleness; never edit bundle rather than source.
- Two old prompt files under public/assets/aistudio may be deployed publicly. Determine intent; move/remove private implementation prompts from production output.

========================================================================================================================
4. TARGET ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION STANDARDS
========================================================================================================================

SINGLE SOURCE OF BUSINESS TRUTH
- Define canonical domain services for identity, membership, tenant, projects, tasks, requests, incidents, goals, CRM, vendors, assets, knowledge, meetings, workflows, notifications, audit, billing, entitlements, finance and AI.
- Frontend calls typed service/API layer, not duplicated business rules embedded in inline handlers.
- Separate DemoDataProvider from live provider. No automatic silent fallback between them.
- Thin Express/Netlify/Firebase adapters call shared services.
- Use explicit domain types plus runtime schemas. TypeScript declarations do not validate request bodies.

AUTHORIZATION
- Verify Firebase ID token on every protected API; derive UID only from token.
- Resolve active tenant membership server-side; ignore body role/org/owner identity assertions.
- Central permission matrix for OWNER, ORG_ADMIN, MANAGER, MEMBER, VIEWER, platform admin.
- Reject suspended/disabled/deleted/pending/expired/revoked accounts and memberships.
- Ownership change, member invite/removal, billing, export, bulk operations require elevated authorization, transaction and audit.
- Validate every record reference belongs to same tenant.

DATA AND RULES
- Define canonical org/member status model and org lifecycle.
- Use server timestamps for security fields.
- Use Firestore transaction for invitation redemption, usage limits, approvals, idempotency and status transitions.
- Emulator tests cover allow and deny paths.
- Admin SDK bypasses rules; server services explicitly authorize.
- No arbitrary client writes to billing/platform/audit/webhook/AI consent/AI proposals.

FRONTEND DATA STATES
Every data-backed page supports loading, populated, empty, stale/offline, partial, denied, expired session, timeout, server error, retry, dirty, pending, saved, conflict, archived, pagination states. A blank page must not mask a failed read. Stale cache must be labelled.

API AND ERRORS
For each route define method/path/auth/role/tenant/request schema/response schema/status/rate-limit/idempotency/audit. Use stable error codes: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, TENANT_NOT_FOUND, NOT_FOUND, VALIDATION_ERROR, CONFLICT, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, CONFIGURATION_ERROR, INTERNAL_ERROR. Never leak stack traces. Never report success on swallowed failure. Retry only safe/idempotent operations.

FINANCE
Store money as integer minor units with ISO currency. Never mix currencies without rate/source/time. No float monetary arithmetic. Validate NaN/Infinity/negative/overflow. Define MRR/ARR/burn/runway/status filters/time period and show insufficient data when source missing.

AI
Load authorized minimum data server-side only after auth/membership/consent. Enforce rate/budget/timeouts/payload limits. Label generated material. Provide source record/timestamp provenance. Model cannot mutate DB. Use typed proposals, strict allowlist and explicit human approval. Never invent IDs/numbers/records/states.

WORKFLOWS
Differentiate authoring/draft/publish/simulation/live execution. Save actual graph; validate before publication. Implement worker only if supported. Otherwise show execution unavailable. Real worker requires per-step idempotency, state machine, retries, timeout, cancellation, secret manager, tenant and permissions.

QUALITY
Run strict typecheck/lint, unit, Firestore rules, API integration, browser E2E, security, concurrency/failure injection, performance and accessibility tests. No release with unresolved P0/P1 or unverified test failures.

9. DOMAIN-SPECIFIC ACCEPTANCE CONTRACTS
========================================================================================================================

AUTH: initial auth state is UNKNOWN, never owner. No private content before auth+membership. Token refresh failure clears private data. Signout stops listeners/requests. UID/org change clears caches and AI history. Demo persona never changes Firebase currentUser. Protected direct navigation is denied.

MEMBERSHIP: path UID/org match; active membership and active org required; known role enum; no OWNER inferred from missing data; removed members lose access immediately; role changes invalidate cache.

CREATE: client usability validation + server schema validation; auth/tenant/permission; same-tenant references; atomically enforce limits; server ID/time; write then canonical response; audit; failure -> no phantom row/success; idempotent retry -> one record.

UPDATE: load existing record; allowed field list; immutable fields protected; optimistic version; legal transition; atomic write+audit; missing record -> NOT_FOUND not upsert; conflict visible.

DELETE: exact target confirm; server permission; retention/reference checks; soft delete if required; audit; idempotent; no stale list row.

APPROVAL: server rechecks active approver, role, separation policy, pending status and version; write decision/actor/time/comment atomically; notification after commit; duplicate approval cannot double-apply; reopen explicit.

INCIDENT: explicit state machine; enum severity/impact; real responders; resolution summary; evidence-backed claims; immutable timeline.

WORKFLOW: versioned graph, unique typed nodes/valid edges, deterministic node deletion, full graph draft, validation before publish, simulation has no side effects, live requires real worker, every step has status and idempotency.

FINANCE: minor units, explicit currency, grouping by currency, documented MRR/ARR/burn/runway, actual source and period, no fabricated fallback, refunds/credits/failures separated, deterministic rounding.

AI PROPOSAL: real source record, verified tenant, allowlisted fields, authorized human, fresh document version, expiry, atomic/idempotent apply, durable decline, provenance, never treat model text as authority.

DIAGNOSTIC: actual executable check, PASS only if every assertion passes, FAIL on failure, WARN degraded, SKIP with reason and not counted as pass, no aggregate conceals critical failure, export actual evidence/no secrets, non-mutating.

ACCESSIBILITY: every control named, dialogs correctly labelled, focus enters and returns, Escape predictable, labelled inputs/errors, color not sole signal, keyboard operation, suitable touch targets, reduced motion, semantic tables/chart descriptions.
